name: Notewise speaker identity
description: Tells your local Notewise engine who is speaking in a meeting. Sends names and speaking times only — never audio, video, or chat.

_comments.permissions: Empty on purpose. This extension reads the participant roster of a page the user is already on and posts to loopback. It needs no tabCapture, no storage, no scripting, and no activeTab — see README.md.
_comments.host_permissions: Loopback only, and ten ports. The engine takes the first free one in that window because a `notewise serve` may already hold the first; a Manifest V3 list is static and cannot name a port chosen at runtime. Verified as Notewise via /health before anything is sent, so a name is never posted to unrelated software that happens to be listening. They apply to the service worker only: a content script's request is the meeting page's, and Chrome refuses a public page's request to loopback whatever the manifest says.
_comments.background: The one place the engine is called from. Content scripts ask it by message (src/relay.js), because their own fetches are attributed to the meeting page and blocked.
_comments.all_frames: The roster is in the top frame. Injecting into subframes would duplicate every observation.
_comments.web_accessible_resources: A Manifest V3 content script is not a module, so content.js reaches these by dynamic import. Scoped to the four meeting origins rather than <all_urls> so no other site can load them. engine.js is not among them: only the worker loads it.
